This claim was based on his status as the eldest son of James Francis Edward Stuart, himself the son of James VII and II. The uprising ended in defeat at the Battle of Culloden, effectively terminating the Jacobite cause.  Jacobites supported the Stuart claim because they hoped for religious toleration for Roman Catholics and because they believed in the divine right of kings. In 1759 he was involved in a French plan to invade Britain, which was abandoned after British naval victories.»
